data.body:
MERGED AND CONFIRMED BY OBSERVATION. Both halves of the operator's requirement — 'project config must be updated to use Bedrock AND local rebar use of Bedrock must be confirmed' — are now evidenced, and the second half is the one that needed a real run rather than a config read.

MERGE: 1336 reached LLM-Review=+1 and Verified=+1 with 0 unresolved comments and merged as 5bc3a432d7 'd2ce: default local dev to Bedrock' (SHA re-derived by trailer, since Gerrit rewrites on submit). rebar.toml now carries [llm] at :154 and [llm.model_classes] at :157.

HALF ONE — CONFIGURATION, verified at the merged commit in a clean env with every REBAR_LLM_* var and REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE explicitly UNSET, so the resolution comes purely from the project file:
    frontier -> bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8
    standard -> bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6
    trivial  -> bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0
Before the change, the identical command at the identical commit-minus-one returned anthropic:claude-opus-4-8 / -sonnet-4-6 / -haiku-4-5. That is the measurement this ticket was filed on, now inverted.

HALF TWO — LOCAL USE, CONFIRMED BY A REAL GATE, not a synthetic call. I ran 'rebar review-plan 129e-2d88-cce2-492c' from a worktree at the merged commit with REBAR_USAGE_LOG set and all REBAR_LLM_* overrides unset. It completed: verdict PASS, 0 blocking, 2 advisory, exit 0 — so a parseable verdict came back through the whole local gate on Bedrock, not merely a provider construction. The per-call tally, 5 records:
    02:23:15  bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8                  in=6282  out=449  plan-reviewer
    02:23:17  bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6                in=4515  out=9    plan-review-prerequisite-verifier
    02:23:19  bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6                in=7842  out=9    plan-review-verifier
    02:23:22  bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6                in=2705  out=75   plan-review-coach
    02:24:27  bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0   in=9111  out=646  ticket-digest
  provider prefix tally: {'bedrock': 5}.  ANY direct-anthropic call: False.
  All THREE classes were exercised locally — frontier on the opus profile, standard on sonnet across three verifier/coach passes, trivial on haiku — so this is not a single-path proof. And it was a review that was genuinely wanted rather than spend for its own sake: 129e's plan is the one being implemented right now, and it came back PASS.

ONE HONEST CAVEAT: cache_read_tokens is 0 on ALL FIVE calls, unlike the production review-bot runs which showed cache reads of 386204 / 308003 / 149162. I am NOT claiming prompt caching was exercised locally. The likely reason is benign and already documented in this repo — these are short one-off calls whose stable prefix sits under the model's 1024-token cache minimum, the condition structured_run.py:490 warns about explicitly — but I did not measure that, so it stands as unverified. Local caching behaviour is out of this ticket's scope (its criteria ask for provider resolution and use, not cache efficacy), and [rebar:1aa2-37cf-5cdf-48b7] already recorded caching engaging on Bedrock for the local gates under its own criteria.

ALL FIVE ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA MET: the decision and its onboarding cost are recorded (operator chose project-default Bedrock over a loud opt-in, and the cost — local gates now need working AWS credentials — is stated in the docs and in this ticket); rebar.toml carries the class table with ids byte-equal to .github/llm-providers/bedrock.toml, pinned two-sided by a test that was mutation-verified from BOTH sides plus class-set equality; a clean checkout resolves all three to bedrock: ids, recorded above as observed output; docs/local-dev-env.md now documents the OPT-OUT rather than presenting Bedrock as opt-in, and the opt-out is exercised by a test that points REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE at the anthropic overlay and asserts resolution returns to anthropic: (verified RED by inverting it); and the epic-level claim needed no correction because it appears NOWHERE in epic 061c or any tracked file — it originated in a git-ignored local handoff note, which is recorded above rather than silently dropped.

ALSO WORTH CARRYING: the scalar '[llm] model' was set alongside the class table, and that was load-bearing rather than belt-and-braces. cfg.model is a second resolution path the class table cannot reach; left unset it defaults to the bare literal 'claude-opus-4-8' and infers provider anthropic. Measured at the merged commit: cfg.model now resolves to bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8. Classes-only would have left the f124 ambient-default leak open in local dev.
